analysis: The tape's narrative flipped inside 30 minutes: August PCE printed cooler than expected (headline 0.3% m/m vs 0.4% expected; y/y 2.6% after a downwardly revised 3.4% July), and futures, which were red at 7:20am ET, rallied on lower yields with October hike odds dropping to ~43%. One caution the headlines bury: the big y/y headline drop is mostly the BEA's methodology revision (software, portfolio management fees, legal services re-measured; data revised back to 2021), not fresh August disinflation — core PCE is still 3.0% y/y, a full point above target, and consumer spending surged 0.9%, so the economy is running hot underneath. That means the dovish read is real but partial: Williams's 'no urgency' plus a soft print buys time, but Friday's jobs report now carries even more weight for October 28. The AI-skepticism crescendo from yesterday (Burry's 'tank hard' broadside with disclosed memory puts, Gates's cyber/bio risk warning, DeepSeek-Huawei CUDA challenge) still hangs over multiples — but tonight is the live test: Micron after the close, with consensus near $51B revenue (+~350% y/y) and EPS ~$31.60 (+~940%), and options pricing a 7-10% swing. Boeing's $20B Navy F/A-XX win is a real defense-sector rotation event (BA +~3% premarket, NOC -4.3%), the kind of headline that matters for sector breadth if the open follows through. Noise to discount: the conflicting premarket megacap-quote snapshots floating around; stick with the Reuters 5:27am ET read (NVDA/GOOGL/AAPL higher, AMD/MRVL lower). What changed vs the 5am brief: futures went from red (-0.15% S&P at 7:20 ET) to rallying post-PCE; the headline PCE 2.6% print replaces the 3.7% consensus expectation.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: August PCE came in cooler than expected: headline +0.3% m/m vs +0.4% forecast; 2.6% y/y after July was revised down to 3.4% (previously 3.7%). Core PCE +0.2% m/m and 3.0% y/y (July core revised to 3.0% from 3.3%). Consumer spending surged 0.9%. The BEA changed its methodology for software, portfolio-management fees and legal services, revising inflation data back to 2021. S&P 500 futures rallied as the 10-year yield fell; October hike odds dropped to ~43% from ~68% Tuesday morning (CME FedWatch).
headlines.why_it_matters: A soft headline print plus spending strength is the dovish combo the market wanted — it validates Williams's 'no urgency' and keeps October hike odds falling. Caveat: the y/y drop is mostly the BEA revision, not August disinflation, so a hot Friday jobs report can still re-priced the hike.

headlines.headline: Micron reports fiscal Q4 after the close today. Consensus: revenue ~$50.9-51.2B (+~350% y/y), adjusted EPS ~$31.5-31.6 (+~940% y/y) on exploding HBM demand for AI servers; Micron's own guide was revenue $50B +/- $1B, EPS $31 +/- $1, ~86% gross margin. Citi raised its price target to $1,300 and UBS reiterated $1,625 ahead of the print; options price a ~7-10% post-print swing. The stock is near $1,080 after nearly quadrupling this year.
headlines.why_it_matters: Tonight is the AI-hardware verdict: memory commentary tests Burry's short thesis against record DRAM-equipment demand. With estimates this extreme, the reaction will be on guidance and 2027 demand durability, not the beat itself.

headlines.headline: The Navy awarded Boeing a contract worth more than $20B to develop its sixth-generation F/A-XX fighter, beating Northrop Grumman (Lockheed Martin exited the race last year). Boeing now holds both sixth-gen fighter programs after winning the Air Force's F-47 in 2025. Boeing shares rose ~2.6-3% in premarket to ~$192.49; Northrop fell ~4.3% to ~$482.94.
headlines.why_it_matters: RBC called it a near-complete reversal of Boeing's defense trajectory — the stock had faced a credible risk of exiting fighter production altogether. Real sector rotation signal: defense names bid while Northrop gets sold on the loss.

headlines.headline: Tesla secured $30B in new credit lines Tuesday: a $20B three-year delayed-draw term loan from Citibank, an $8B five-year revolver from Wells Fargo, and a $2B 364-day revolver. Tesla said it does not plan to draw on them this year; it projects at least $25B of 2026 capex to scale Cybercab, Optimus and the Semi. Separately, Tesla's deadline to respond to NHTSA's audit of its Cybercab FMVSS self-certification (steering/braking standards that assume a human driver) is today.
headlines.why_it_matters: A $30B liquidity backstop de-risks the heavy-capex scaling story for Cybercab/Optimus/Semi — funding is set, execution is the question. The NHTSA deadline is the near-term regulatory watch item for the robotaxi rollout.

headlines.headline: Megacaps were mixed-to-higher ahead of PCE: per Reuters at 5:27am ET, Nvidia, Alphabet and Apple moved higher in premarket while AMD and Marvell ticked lower. Earlier snapshots showed Amazon +~1% and Tesla +0.4% against softness in Meta/Google/Microsoft. Yesterday's confirmed Meta Jefferies Buy/$875 note and Nvidia's $150B buyback expansion remain the tape's bullish megacap anchors.
headlines.why_it_matters: Megacap breadth is hesitant but intact — no single name is breaking down into the open, with the PCE relief bid supporting growth multiples ahead of Micron tonight.

headlines.headline: Futures swung from red to a post-PCE rally: Dow E-minis -0.2% and S&P 500 E-minis -0.15% at 7:20am ET (per the prior reading) recovered after the soft print on lower yields, with Nasdaq 100 futures at -0.32% pre-data per Barron's. Overnight Asia was up (Nikkei +1.94%, Shanghai +0.31%); 10Y at 5.24% pre-PCE (down from 5.29% Tuesday high), gold ~$4,215, WTI ~$90.80, bitcoin ~$83,800.
headlines.why_it_matters: The tape refused to commit until the data, then rallied on it — classic pre-data positioning chop. The reversal confirms the open is data-dependent: a weak October-hike repricing would flip the bid just as fast.
